title: Finding the right style. Light and movements
author: GeorgiaWitness1
selftext:
**First forget the movements of the characters,** will take 10 20x CC subs to make this work well 

  
In terms of contrast, fight and overall look, would you say that is acceptable? The first one is my tutorial fight, dry color lighting. The second is more rich, more over the top colors and stuff moving around. 

  
I'm struggling with style definition across the game. Would you prefer 1 or 2?

replies.author: GeorgiaWitness1
replies.body:
yes i build a skill and workflow. 

How it works:

1. Generate scene image (Gemini)  
2. Run quality check  
3. Generate layers in Codex queue layer separation. The layers are generated in separate images, by breaking the image apart. Quality Gate  
4. Bring the layers together  
5. Bring the physics in Unity (i.e light, water and so on)  
6. Quality gate

This runs in Gauntlet Loop style until looks good. 

All in low effort is enough usually

replies.author: Tyalou
replies.body: The resolution is not consistent across, OP uses icons that are squished into their buttons and the characters are "too detailed" for how they are rendered on screen. It needs an overall pass on assets resolution across the board. It's a bunch of AI generated images generated at the same resolution and then scaled up/down for where OP needed them. I see a lot of work went into it but sadly it's a massive pass for me.

replies.author: GeorgiaWitness1
